glosses: To cover with a thin layer of gold; to cover with gold leaf.

examples.text: High above the city, on a tall column, stood the statue of the Happy Prince. He was gilded all over with thin leaves of fine gold, for eyes he had two bright sapphires, and a large red ruby glowed on his sword-hilt.

I will make fast the doors, and gild myself
 With some more ducats, and be with you straight.

glosses: To decorate with a golden surface appearance.

examples.text: Gild the entire outside with beaten egg yolk, and sprinkle it with grated parmesan.

glosses: To give a bright or pleasing aspect to.

examples.text: When sparkling stars twire not, thou gild'st the even.

glosses: To give a brilliant colour or flush to one's face; (also) to make appear drunk.

examples.text:
[Alonso] And Trinculo is reeling-ripe: vvhere sſhould they
Finde this grand Liquor that hath gilded'em?
Hovv cam'ſt thou in this pickle?
No trade gild might be started without the consent of the whole body of hanasters, who would insist that the regulations were not harmful to the burgesses as a whole; […]

glosses: Revêtir un objet d’une mince pellicule d’or.

examples.text: Précisément, mademoiselle, la grâce vient des proportions exactes entre les stylobates, les plinthes, les corniches et les ornements ; puis je n’ai rien doré, les couleurs sont sobres et n’offrent point de tons éclatants.
Le jour venait. […]. Les pailles, dont les couches épaisses recouvraient entièrement le sol de la cour, se doraient peu à peu d'un jaune pâle sous la lueur grandissante du crépuscule.
Les moissons commencent à se dorer.
